metadata.dcterms:abstract:
This handbook provides guidance for the implementation of standardized product master data management through national product catalogues (NPCs) to support digital transformation in health supply chains. Developed within the framework of the WHO Digital Implementation Investment Guide and aligned with the SMART Guidelines initiative, the publication outlines regulatory, governance, technological and operational approaches for establishing interoperable product registries and harmonized product information systems. It explains the importance of standardized product master data for ensuring accurate identification, tracking and management of health products across manufacturers, regulatory authorities, procurement entities, warehouses, health facilities and other supply chain stakeholders.
The handbook describes policies and procedures for data governance, coding structures, interoperability standards, change management and capacity-building to support sustainable implementation. It also presents guidance on integrating standardized product master data with digital health, regulatory and supply chain systems to improve forecasting, procurement, inventory management, pharmacovigilance, product recalls and traceability. In addition, the publication highlights mechanisms for sharing product master data as a global good and leveraging WHO-hosted tools and open standards to strengthen coordination, data quality and supply chain efficiency across countries and organizations.
